text:
sophia: Heads-up — we're seeing repeated gRPC streaming stalls between gpu-pool pods in us-west-2 after last night's node-image + SR-IOV rollout. 3 customer jobs lost steady throughput, tail latency spikes.
raj: Any obvious packet drops or NIC errors?
alex: client side shows repeated UNAVAILABLE / stream reset. server logs show long stalls during transmit. tcpdump on pod veth shows lots of large packets followed by ICMP "fragmentation needed" from the host.
maria: That sounds like an MTU path issue across the overlay tunnel. Did OVN or the VPC tunnel MTU change with the new image?
sophia: We enabled SR-IOV on a subset of nodes and bumped host NIC MTU to 9000 to support jumbo frames. OVN tun interface was left at default 1450 on those nodes — looks asymmetric.
alex: Pulled quick outputs from node-12:
```bash
# ip link show
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
72: ovn-k8s0: mtu 1450 qdisc noop state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default
```
and tcpdump snippet from node-12:
```text
17:22:05.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64) 10.10.1.5.52345 > 10.10.2.7.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:32769, ack 1, win 29200, length 32768
17:22:05.123457 ICMP 10.10.2.7 unreachable frag-needed and DF set (mtu = 1450)
```
maria: That explains it — large gRPC messages + DF bit + MTU mismatch = fragmentation blackholing across the OVN tunnel. For streaming workloads (long GPT-like token streams) this is catastrophic.
raj: Any quick mitigations? We need to reduce customer impact and restore throughput fast.
alex: Immediate mitigations we tested on one node:
- Turn off GSO/GRO/TLS offloading on physical NIC for affected pods: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` — reduces large-segment sends, avoids DF triggers.
- Apply TCPMSS clamp at host egress so SYNs advertise smaller MSS: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`
Both restored streaming stability in our quick test (throughput back to ~85% of baseline, tail latency normalizing).
maria: Longer term we should make overlay MTU and host NIC MTU consistent (accounting for tunnel overhead). Options:
1) Set host NIC MTU to 9000 and configure OVN/VPC tunnel MTU to 8972 (9000 - overhead), or
2) Keep host MTU 1500 across all nodes (safer), or
3) Adjust CNI to advertise and enforce matched MTUs at pod-level during provisioning.
sophia: There's also a surfaced RDMA concern: some of the GPU workloads use RoCE across nodes; SR-IOV/VF offloads plus fragmented packets cause RDMA path errors. We need to isolate RDMA-capable nodes from overlay until we have a validated config.
raj: Can we do a rolling fix that doesn't violate customer SLAs? CPU/GPU capacity is tight — evicting pods will disrupt jobs.
alex: Plan proposed:
- Immediate: apply iptables clamp + disable GSO on the subset of 5 nodes that were changed; no pod restarts required.
- Next 24h: update node image to set OVN tun MTU to match host (or set host to 1500) during next maintenance window and coordinate with networking.
- If RDMA jobs still fail, isolate RDMA nodes into a separate pool and avoid overlay (use direct attachment).
maria: Filed a ticket with network team for OVN config change and asked cloud infra to confirm VPC tunnel overhead (GRE/GENEVE). Also flagged kernel upgrade for rollback testing if needed.
infra-bot: INC-2026-312 created (mtu-asymmetry-gpu-streams). Priority P1, assigned to @maria and @alex, scheduled runbook update: https://infra.internal/inc/INC-2026-312
sophia: Thanks — apply clamp and GSO off to the 5 nodes now, keep me posted. I'll message customers for the temporary mitigation note.
raj: After clamp + gso-off applied: monitoring shows stream success rate up, no more ICMP frag-needed. I'll leave the iptables rule persistent via host-config.
maria: Moving to schedule window to standardize MTU across cluster and add MTU checks to node-join pipeline. We'll also add a preflight that fails if host MTU and OVN MTU mismatch > 50 bytes.
sophia: Great. Postmortem incoming after stabilization. For the notes: root cause = asymmetric MTU between SR-IOV-enabled host NICs and overlay tunnel (DF set + large gRPC streaming), exacerbated by kernel + offload behavior. Workarounds = TCPMSS clamp + disable GSO/GRO on affected hosts; long-term = MTU harmonization or CNI enforcement.
